business_summary.text: Orkla India is a multi-category food company with brands such as MTR and Eastern, operating in spices and convenience foods, with 70% of revenue from South India and 21% from international markets.

call_points.text: Management declined to give numeric FY27 guidance, saying only that it aims for double-digit growth and is aligned with analysts' higher aspirations.
International business grew 10.1%, led by GCC at 18.1%; US returned to positive value growth.
Market share gained 30-50 bps in Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, but declined about 30 bps in Kerala.
Management said it has more or less taken all needed price increases but will monitor the dynamic environment.
Volume growth reached 5.9% in FY26, up from 1.8% in FY23, demonstrating strong consumption trends.
Spice prices have bottomed out and started inflating, with Q4 showing a 6.5% uptick.
Cash surplus stood at ₹600 crore as of March 31, 2026, offering flexibility for growth.
EBITDA growth was driven by price management and operating efficiencies, partly offset by freight increases and Project Bolt investments.
GCC business experienced elevated freight costs and increased transit times due to West Asia port closures.

operating_notes.text: Orkla India is targeting bolt-on acquisitions in the ₹300-400 crore range, backed by internal cash flows and a debt-free balance sheet.
MTR Foods launched its Minute Fresh Batter range (Dosa and Rice Rava Idli batters) in Hyderabad.
Digital commerce contributed 8.7% to domestic sales in FY26, growing 38% YoY.
FY26 volume growth reached 5.9%, the highest in the past 4 years.
Spices prices saw a 6.5% uptick in Q4 FY26 after two years of deflation.
Digital commerce grew 38% YoY in FY26, contributing 8.7% of domestic revenues.
Spice inflation was 32.8% YoY in Q1FY27, with chilli up 78% and coriander up 40%.
Digital commerce contributed 8.9% of domestic revenue in Q1FY27, up from 7.2% a year ago, with a 60:40 convenience foods to spices mix.
Kerala distribution restructuring delivered 14% sales productivity improvement and 6% effective coverage increase in Q1FY27.
Mr. Atle Vidar Nagel Johansen resigned as Chairman & Non-Executive Director and Ms. Maria Syse-Nybraaten was appointed as Chairperson of the Board.

timeline.summary: Orkla India's MD outlined plans for bolt-on acquisitions of ₹300-400 crore and a strategic focus on convenience foods.
Orkla India announced the voting results of its postal ballot on April 27, 2026, approving the remuneration for Chairman Atle Vidar Nagel Johansen.
Orkla India launched its MTR Minute Fresh Batter range in Hyderabad, expanding its convenience food portfolio.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹625.8 Cr, net profit ₹73.44 Cr.
Orkla India presented its Q4FY26 investor presentation highlighting 6.2% product sales growth and 16.0% EBITDA margin.
Orkla India reported FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹2,509 crore, up 4.8% YoY, and EBITDA of ₹424 crore.
Orkla India Limited hosted a conference call with analysts/investors on May 19, 2026, from 5:00 PM to 6:08 PM (IST) discussing audited FY2025-26 results.
Orkla India reported Q4FY26 revenue of ₹626 Cr, up 5% YoY, and full-year FY26 revenue of ₹2,509 Cr.
Orkla India reported Q1FY27 revenue up 10.4% to ₹659 Cr and EBITDA margin of 17.5%, with volume growth of 1.7% as spice inflation of 32.8% was passed through via 11.4% price hikes.

Orkla India reconstituted its Nomination and Remuneration Committee and Stakeholders Relationship Committee following the resignation of Chairman Atle Vidar Nagel Johansen and appointment of Maria Syse-Nybraaten as Chairperson in October 2026.

watchlist.response: Sanjay Sharma disagreed, pointing to 6.3% domestic volume growth excluding Kerala and said delivering 5-6% volume growth is substantial.
watchlist.text: Volume growth of 4.4% excluding Kerala seems underwhelming in an inflationary environment.

watchlist.response: Sanjay Sharma explained the entrepreneur ran Eastern for the first three years post-acquisition, a new CEO was appointed in January 2025, and the project started in February 2026; the West Asia crisis and commodity inflation were not anticipated.
watchlist.text: Why was Kerala distribution restructuring not done before the IPO, burdening minority shareholders?

watchlist.response: Management said it aims for double-digit growth and is aligned with analysts' higher aspirations but does not give forward-looking guidance.
watchlist.text: What is the growth aspiration versus GDP growth?

watchlist.response: CFO said it is too early to confirm eligibility and will track growth; FY26-27 is the last year of the scheme.
